newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - U.S. gasoline stocks shortfall widens.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - U.S. gasoline stocks shortfall widens.

text.p: A shortfall in gasoline inventories widened this week and refiners will be racing to build stocks back up to last year's levels ahead of the spring and summer driving season, analysts said on Tuesday.

Early maintenance turnarounds also trimmed output at U.S. refineries and contributed to a draw in heating oil stocks last week, analysts said following release of the American Petroleum Institute weekly petroleum stocks survey.
Gasoline inventories rose a modest 415,000 barrels nationwide on the week, but the shortfall compared to last year widened to 9.35 million barrels from 6.5 million barrels, API said.

"(Gasoline stocks) are 9.3 million barrels below last year's levels going into one of the heaviest maintenance seasons in a while," Merrill Lynch broker Dee Dee Finley said. "It's going to be difficult for gas to build back up."

Gasoline imports soared to 507,000 bpd last week, up from 207,000 bpd the previous week and from 300,000 bpd in the same week last year. Also, shipping agents say there is a surge of imports due to head from Europe in the weeks ahead, with at least 7.5 million barrels scheduled to load there in the second half of this month.

Domestic refineries, which had been running at a blistering pace to build up heating oil stocks during the autumn, were running at 90.7 percent of capacity in the week ended January 10 due to turnarounds and outage, analysts said.
Distillate stocks nationwide were drawn down 1.29 million barrels, ending the week a scant 350,000 barrels shy of last year's levels, the Washington, D.C. trade group said.
In the key PADD I region, taking in the northeast heating oil market, heating oil stocks fell 309,000 last week but the year-on-year deficit in stocks narrowed by around half to 3.2 million barrels.

As demand eased on moderated weather in the U.S. Northeast, several U.S. Gulf Coast refineries rang in the New Year with early planned maintenance turnarounds, analysts said. "It's probably the main reason why distillates managed to fall," ING Futures and Options Inc analyst Tom Bentz said.
The narrowing gap in year-to-year distillate stocks also reflected a 5.8 million distillate draw posted in the same week last year, Bentz said.
With more than 45 percent of the U.S. heating oil draw of 1.8 million barrels occuring in the Gulf Coast, much of it from exports, traders viewed the draw as bearish.
"East Coast demand stinks. I wouldn't buy the market," one Gulf Coast trader said.

Crude oil stocks nationwide remained 14.03 million barrels below last year's levels despite a 4.65 million barrel build on the week, API said. The crude build was concentrated in the Gulf Coast, where lower refinery throughput left crude stocks 3.12 million barrels higher on the week.

Crude imports rose to 7.65 million barrels per day, up an average 1.64 million barrels per day on the week. Refined product imports rose to 2.09 million barrels, up an average 203,000 barrels per day, API said.
